title: Home guide: germinating seeds release heat
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 106 (Home practical guide and safety card: germinating seeds (portal worksheet; dried peas or lentils, no disinfectant at home))
intro: Read it all first, then do it with an adult nearby.

practical.aim: Show that respiring (germinating) seeds release energy as heat.
equipment: Two bowls and kitchen roll or a damp cloth
A thermometer if you have one
safety: Do not eat the soaked seeds; wash your hands
An adult knows what you are doing and stays nearby
Clear a space; tidy up and wash your hands afterwards
method: Soak two bowls of dried peas or lentils overnight.
Next day, boil one bowl (an adult) to kill the seeds; let it cool to room temperature. These are the control.
Wrap each set in a damp cloth inside an insulated cup with a thermometer.
Record the temperature of both every few hours for two days.
Compare: the living seeds should become warmer.
practical.adult: Adult step: boiling the control seeds.
